newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Over 1,000 protest China civil liberty curbs in HK.
newsitem.headline: Over 1,000 protest China civil liberty curbs in HK.

text.p: Over 1,000 Hong Kong people took to the streets on Sunday to protest against curbs on civil liberties which future leader Tung Chee-hwa plans to enforce when China takes over at midnight on June 30.
If Tung's plans go ahead, from July 1 local political groups will be banned from taking foreign donations and police permission must be given before demonstrations can be held.
At present, police need only be notified of planned demonstrations.
Tung, who launched the plans early this month, has invited the public to submit comments on the changes by the end of April.

But protesters on Sunday called the consultation a sham. Brandishing bright red and green banners, they chanted "No to fake consultation" as they marched from Victoria Park to the Central business district.
The march was organised by the Hong Kong People's Alliance for Human Rights, comprising 30 local non-governmental organisations.

More than 150 years of British rule over Hong Kong are due to end at midnight on June 30, when the colony reverts to China. Many of the territory's 6.4 million people are concerned about a loss of civil liberties and democratic institutions after the handover.
